name: Dusky Orient Blue
lede: Dusky Orient Blue is a dark, greenish blue plotted in Ridgway's 1912 atlas and later carried into the ISCC-NBS dictionary, close to the blue called petrol.

sections.title: From Ridgway's plate to the 1955 dictionary
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 atlas places this hue on plate XXXIV at hue 45′′, tone m [1]. The scan of that plate is aged and only an approximation of the original pigment [1]. The ISCC-NBS circular of 1955 absorbs it into block 186, naming the region grayish blue, Munsell notation 5.1B 3.5/3.5 [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dark-chessylite-blue]], [[connor-s-lakefront]], [[dark-delft-blue]] and [[patent-blue]], at 2.5, 2.8, 3.7 and 3.9 ΔE [2]. Dusky Orient Blue sits darker and greener than a plain [[blue]], on the green side [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of this one covers at least five percent of the canvas in 133 paintings, about 0.6 percent overall, as photographed [4]. It is strongest in the 1530s, at five times the archive's average rate, and again among Post-Impressionists, where Paul Cezanne and Auguste Renoir each use it well above average [4]. It shares a canvas most often with [[petrol]], and after that with charcoal grays [4]. These counts read photographs of varnished paintings, not pigments [4].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a systematic grid name (Ridgway) and a dictionary name (ISCC-NBS), not a documented place
